claims.title: First settlement of New Guinea
claims.summary: People crossed from Southeast Asia to the joined landmass of Sahul, settling New Guinea in some of the earliest sea voyages and beginning one of the longest continuous human occupations on Earth.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-50000bce-first-settlement-of-new-guinea, claim TL:PNG:event:50000bce:first-settlement-of-new-guinea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independent invention of agriculture at Kuk
claims.summary: In the highland swamp of Kuk, communities drained wetlands to cultivate taro and bananas, one of only a few places on Earth where farming arose independently — recognised by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

sources.label: Kuk Early Agricultural Site — World Heritage List

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-5000bce-independent-invention-of-agriculture-at-kuk, claim TL:PNG:event:5000bce:independent-invention-of-agriculture-at-kuk, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Austronesian speakers reach the coasts
claims.summary: A major migration of Austronesian-speaking peoples settles the coastal regions, layering a seafaring, trading world over the far older interior one.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-500bce-austronesian-speakers-reach-the-coasts, claim TL:PNG:event:500bce:austronesian-speakers-reach-the-coasts, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: More than 800 languages emerge
claims.summary: Rugged terrain and long isolation gave rise to over 800 distinct languages and more than a thousand ethnic groups, making New Guinea the most linguistically diverse region in the world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1000bce-more-than-800-languages-emerge, claim TL:PNG:event:1000bce:more-than-800-languages-emerge, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The first European visitor
claims.summary: The Portuguese sailor Jorge de Meneses reaches the islands and calls them the ilhas dos Papuas; twenty years later a Spaniard names the main island New Guinea for its resemblance to the African coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1526-the-first-european-visitor, claim TL:PNG:event:1526:the-first-european-visitor, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kula ring and the trading seas
claims.summary: Substantial exchange networks operate across New Guinea, the most extensive of them the Kula ring — a ceremonial circuit of shell valuables spanning hundreds of kilometres of open water.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1800-the-kula-ring-and-the-trading-seas, claim TL:PNG:event:1800:the-kula-ring-and-the-trading-seas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Traders, missionaries, and labour recruiters arrive
claims.summary: Whalers, plume hunters, and beche-de-mer traders worked the coasts, missionaries founded stations, and labour recruiters — including coercive 'blackbirders' — drew Melanesian workers to plantations in Queensland and Fiji.

sources.label: Papua New Guinea: forty years of independence
sources.publisher: State Library of New South Wales

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1873-traders-missionaries-and-labour-recruiters, claim TL:PNG:event:1873:traders-missionaries-and-labour-recruiters, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The island is partitioned
claims.summary: Germany proclaimed a protectorate over the north-east (German New Guinea) and Britain over the southern coast (British New Guinea) within days of each other, splitting eastern New Guinea between two empires.

sources.label: Papua New Guinea — The colonial period

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1884-the-island-is-partitioned, claim TL:PNG:event:1884:the-island-is-partitioned, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gold on the Mambare
claims.summary: A strike on the Mambare River brings a gold rush and with it hostilities between miners and the people whose land they worked.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1895-gold-on-the-mambare, claim TL:PNG:event:1895:gold-on-the-mambare, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Australia takes over Papua
claims.summary: Following the Papua Act of 1905, British New Guinea became the Australian Territory of Papua, and formal Australian administration began in 1906.

sources.label: Papua New Guinea — The colonial period

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1906-australia-takes-over-papua, claim TL:PNG:event:1906:australia-takes-over-papua, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Australia occupies German New Guinea
claims.summary: At the outbreak of the First World War, Australian forces seized German New Guinea, ending German colonial rule in the region.

sources.label: Papua New Guinea — The colonial period

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1914-australia-occupies-german-new-guinea, claim TL:PNG:event:1914:australia-occupies-german-new-guinea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: League of Nations mandate over New Guinea
claims.summary: Australia received a Class C League of Nations mandate to administer the former German territory as the Territory of New Guinea, governed from Rabaul and kept separate from Papua.

sources.label: Papua New Guinea — The colonial period

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1921-league-of-nations-mandate-over-new-guinea, claim TL:PNG:event:1921:league-of-nations-mandate-over-new-guinea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bulolo gold rush
claims.summary: A major find along the Bulolo river draws a second rush, pulling outsiders and aircraft into country that had barely been mapped.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1926-the-bulolo-gold-rush, claim TL:PNG:event:1926:the-bulolo-gold-rush, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First contact in the highlands
claims.summary: Australian prospectors and patrol officers walked into the central highlands and found densely populated farming valleys — perhaps a million people — entirely unknown to the outside world until then.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1933-first-contact-in-the-highlands, claim TL:PNG:event:1933:first-contact-in-the-highlands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kokoda Track campaign
claims.summary: Australian and Papuan troops halted the Japanese advance over the Owen Stanley Range toward Port Moresby and drove them back; over 600 Australians were killed in arguably Australia's most significant campaign of the war.

sources.label: Australians in the Kokoda Track Campaign, 21 July to 16 November 1942
sources.publisher: Anzac Portal, Australian Department of Veterans' Affairs

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1942-the-kokoda-track-campaign, claim TL:PNG:event:1942:the-kokoda-track-campaign, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Papuan carriers and soldiers
claims.summary: Papuan carriers moved supplies and the wounded across the mountains, and soldiers of the Papuan Infantry Battalion fought alongside Australian forces throughout the New Guinea campaigns.

sources.label: Australians in the Kokoda Track Campaign, 21 July to 16 November 1942
sources.publisher: Anzac Portal, Australian Department of Veterans' Affairs

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1942-papuan-carriers-and-soldiers, claim TL:PNG:event:1942:papuan-carriers-and-soldiers, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bougainville campaign
claims.summary: More than 30,000 Australians fought a long campaign of patrols and small actions on Bougainville, with over 500 killed, until the Japanese garrison surrendered in August 1945.

sources.label: Australians in the Kokoda Track Campaign, 21 July to 16 November 1942
sources.publisher: Anzac Portal, Australian Department of Veterans' Affairs

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1944-the-bougainville-campaign, claim TL:PNG:event:1944:the-bougainville-campaign, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Papua and New Guinea united
claims.summary: Australia combined its administration of Papua and the former German mandate into a single Territory of Papua and New Guinea, with the north held as a United Nations trust territory.

sources.label: Papua New Guinea — The colonial period

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1945-papua-and-new-guinea-united, claim TL:PNG:event:1945:papua-and-new-guinea-united, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The first elections with indigenous voters
claims.summary: Papuans and New Guineans vote for the first time, sixteen years after the two territories were joined under one administration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1961-the-first-elections-with-indigenous-voters, claim TL:PNG:event:1961:the-first-elections-with-indigenous-voters, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: West New Guinea transferred to Indonesia
claims.summary: The United Nations hands control of the island's western half to Indonesia; the two governments agree the position of their shared border ten years later.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1963-west-new-guinea-transferred-to-indonesia, claim TL:PNG:event:1963:west-new-guinea-transferred-to-indonesia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: An elected indigenous majority
claims.summary: A 64-member House of Assembly replaces the Legislative Council, and for the first time indigenous representatives hold most of the seats.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1964-an-elected-indigenous-majority, claim TL:PNG:event:1964:an-elected-indigenous-majority, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The country is named Papua New Guinea
claims.summary: The two territories that two empires had drawn take a single name, four years before they take a flag.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1971-the-country-is-named-papua-new-guinea, claim TL:PNG:event:1971:the-country-is-named-papua-new-guinea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Internal self-government
claims.summary: Papua New Guinea achieved internal self-government with Michael Somare as chief minister, a peaceful step toward full independence from Australia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1973-internal-self-government, claim TL:PNG:event:1973:internal-self-government, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence
claims.summary: Papua New Guinea became an independent nation under Prime Minister Michael Somare; Australia transferred sovereignty and the United States recognised the new state the same day.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Papua New Guinea
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1975-independence, claim TL:PNG:event:1975:independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bougainville conflict
claims.summary: A secessionist war over the Panguna mine, land, and environmental damage pitted Bougainvillean rebels against the PNG Defence Force; death-toll estimates range widely, commonly cited at roughly 10,000–20,000 and treated as estimates.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1988-the-bougainville-conflict, claim TL:PNG:event:1988:the-bougainville-conflict, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sandline, the mutiny and the Burnham Truce
claims.summary: The government hires mercenaries to reinforce its troops on Bougainville, provoking a mutiny in its own army; the Burnham Truce later that year ends the decade of armed struggle.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-1997-sandline-the-mutiny-and-the-burnham-truce, claim TL:PNG:event:1997:sandline-the-mutiny-and-the-burnham-truce, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bougainville Peace Agreement
claims.summary: Following a 1998 ceasefire, a peace agreement created the Autonomous Region of Bougainville and promised a future referendum on the island's political status.

sources.label: The Bougainville referendum and beyond
sources.publisher: University of Melbourne, Laureate Program in Comparative Constitutional Law

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Papua New Guinea: From the world's first farmers and 800 languages to a young Pacific nation.", terralore.co/country/PNG/chronicle#ev-2001-bougainville-peace-agreement, claim TL:PNG:event:2001:bougainville-peace-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bougainville independence referendum
claims.summary: Bougainvilleans voted about 98 per cent for independence over greater autonomy; the non-binding result must be negotiated with PNG and ratified by its parliament.

sources.label: The Bougainville referendum and beyond
sources.publisher: University of Melbourne, Laureate Program in Comparative Constitutional Law

sources.label: Bougainville votes overwhelmingly for independence from Papua New Guinea
